content: The term FODMAP stands for Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monosaccharides, and Polyols. FODMAPs are short-chain carbohydrates and polyols that are poorly absorbed in the gastrointestinal tract but are highly fermentable by gut bacteria. A low FODMAP diet has been shown to be potentially effective in managing symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), as evidenced by a systematic review of randomized controlled trials and a more recent clinical trial. One of the studies included in the systematic review evaluated the combined effects of a low FODMAP diet and a diet high in dietary fiber. A diet that is low in FODMAPs but rich in soluble fiber often incorporates psyllium, also known as ispaghula husks, as a source of fiber. A specific high-fiber, low FODMAP diet has been developed, which provides approximately 23 grams of fiber and 3 grams of FODMAPs per day. Symptoms of gluten sensitivity in individuals who do not have celiac disease may, in fact, be caused by the presence of fructans in wheat rather than gluten itself.
